scope: Deuteronomy 7–12, all 161 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 7–11 and 12:1–31 align directly; public 12:32 binds Hebrew 13:1. All 161 original XML records are hashed in full, including the numbering note.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps all seven named peoples and the comparative strength within the opening condition.
verses.before: “When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess and clears away many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you—
verses.after: “When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess and drives out many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you—
verses.tsw_comparator: “When the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess and clears away many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than you—

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic ban and absence of mercy; the condition continues from verse 1 without disguising destruction as mere relocation.
verses.before: and when the LORD your God gives them before you and you strike them, you will devote them completely to destruction. You will make no covenant with them and show them no favor.
verses.after: and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, you must devote them completely to destruction. Make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
verses.tsw_comparator: and when the LORD your God gives them before you and you strike them, you shall devote them completely to destruction. You shall make no covenant with them and show them no favor.

verses.rationale: Keeps both directions of the marriage prohibition and the specific family relationships.
verses.before: You will not intermarry with them. You will not give your daughter to his son, and you will not take his daughter for your son,
verses.after: Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughter to one of their sons or take one of their daughters for your son.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not intermarry with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter for your son,

verses.rationale: Names the LORD to clarify the Hebrew divine first-person referent within Moses' address, while retaining the singular son and religious reason.
verses.before: for he will turn your son away from following me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you and destroy you quickly.
verses.after: For they will turn your son away from following the LORD to serve other gods. Then the LORD's anger will burn against you, and he will quickly destroy you.
verses.tsw_comparator: for he will turn your son away from following me to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you and destroy you quickly.

verses.rationale: Retains four distinct cultic objects and their corresponding destructive actions.
verses.before: But thus you will do to them: tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images with fire.
verses.after: This is what you must do to them: tear down their altars, smash their standing stones, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images.
verses.tsw_comparator: But thus you shall do to them: tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images with fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps holiness and treasured possession as related descriptions of the chosen community.
verses.before: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be for him a treasured people from all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.
verses.after: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD your God chose you to be his treasured people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be for him a treasured people from all the peoples who are on the face of the ground.

verses.rationale: Makes the negative explanation and corrective statement clear while retaining affection and choice.
verses.before: “It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD desired you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all the peoples.
verses.after: The LORD did not set his affection on you and choose you because you were more numerous than other peoples. You were the fewest of all peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: “It was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples that the LORD desired you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all the peoples.

verses.rationale: Preserves love, sworn obligation, redemption, and both strong-hand and enslaving-hand images.
verses.before: Rather, because the LORD loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors, the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
verses.after: It was because the LORD loved you and kept the oath he swore to your fathers that he brought you out with a strong hand. He redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, because the LORD loved you and kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors, the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit thousand generations and follows the read form of commands, whose written spelling is preserved in the source record.
verses.before: Know therefore that the LORD your God—he is God, the faithful God, keeping covenant and steadfast love with people who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,
verses.after: Know, then, that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God. He keeps covenant and faithful love for a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know therefore that the LORD your God—he is God, the faithful God, keeping covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated face image and destructive repayment without replacing hatred with mere indifference.
verses.before: but repaying people who hate him to their face, to destroy them. He will not delay with one who hates him; to his face he will repay him.
verses.after: But he repays those who hate him to their face, destroying them. He does not delay with anyone who hates him; he repays that person to their face.
verses.tsw_comparator: but repaying those who hate him to their face, to destroy them. He will not delay with one who hates him; to his face he will repay him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the categories of instruction and hearing directed toward action.
verses.before: So you will keep the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that I command you today, to do them.
verses.after: So keep the commandment, statutes, and rulings I give you today, and put them into practice.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you shall keep the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that I command you today, to do them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional relation and the repeated keeping on both sides.
verses.before: “And it will be, because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and steadfast love that he swore to your ancestors.
verses.after: If you listen to these rulings, keep them, and put them into practice, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and faithful love he swore to your fathers.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will be, because you listen to these judgments and keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and steadfast love that he swore to your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Retains the two fruit images, three crops, and both animal groups within the land promise.
verses.before: He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, new wine, and oil, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock, upon the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
verses.after: He will love you, bless you, and make you numerous. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground—your grain, new wine, and oil, the calves of your herds and the young of your flocks—in the land he swore to your fathers to give you.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, new wine, and oil, the offspring of your cattle and the increase of your flock, upon the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.

verses.rationale: Makes both male and female infertility explicit without treating the promise as a diagnosis of individual people's faith.
verses.before: You will be blessed above all peoples. There will not be a barren male or female among you or among your livestock.
verses.after: You will be blessed beyond all peoples. No man or woman among you will be unable to have children, and none of your livestock will be barren.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be blessed above all peoples. There will not be a barren male or female among you or among your livestock.

verses.rationale: Preserves the comprehensive promise and the transfer of disease to enemies with direct divine agency.
verses.before: The LORD will remove from you every sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Egypt that you knew will he place upon you, but he will put them upon everyone who hate you.
verses.after: The LORD will remove every sickness from you. He will not put on you any of the terrible diseases of Egypt that you knew, but will put them on all who hate you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will remove from you every sickness, and none of the evil diseases of Egypt that you knew will he place upon you, but he will put them upon all who hate you.

verses.rationale: Retains devouring and snare as the source's violent and entrapment images.
verses.before: You will consume all the peoples whom the LORD your God gives to you. Your eye will not pity them, and you will not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
verses.after: You must devour all the peoples the LORD your God hands over to you. Do not look on them with pity, and do not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall consume all the peoples whom the LORD your God gives to you. Your eye shall not pity them, and you shall not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the imagined inner speech and collective first-person question.
verses.before: “If you say in your heart, ‘These nations are more numerous than I am; how can I dispossess them?’
verses.after: You may say in your heart, ‘These nations are more numerous than I am. How can I drive them out?’
verses.tsw_comparator: “If you say in your heart, ‘These nations are more numerous than I am; how can I dispossess them?’

verses.rationale: Renders emphatic remembering as remember well and preserves the named precedent.
verses.before: you will not fear them. You will surely remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
verses.after: Do not be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall not fear them. You shall surely remember what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

verses.rationale: Retains every element in the recollection and the explicit comparison with future enemies.
verses.before: the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs, the wonders, the strong hand, and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. So the LORD your God will do to all the peoples whom you fear.
verses.after: You saw the great trials, the signs and wonders, the strong hand and outstretched arm with which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you fear.
verses.tsw_comparator: the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs, the wonders, the strong hand, and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. So the LORD your God will do to all the peoples whom you fear.

verses.rationale: Retains hornets as the traditional concrete reading while noting uncertainty about the term.
verses.before: Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them until people who remain and hide from you perish.
verses.after: The LORD your God will also send hornets among them, until even those who remain and hide from you have perished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, the LORD your God will send the hornet among them until those who remain and hide from you perish.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine presence as the reason for courage and preserves the force of fearsome.
verses.before: You will not be terrified before them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and fearsome God.
verses.after: Do not dread them, because the LORD your God is among you, a great and fearsome God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not be terrified before them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and fearsome God.

verses.rationale: Preserves gradual removal and its ecological reason without harmonizing the quick destruction language elsewhere.
verses.before: The LORD your God will clear away these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to finish them quickly, lest the wild animals multiply against you.
verses.after: The LORD your God will drive these nations out before you little by little. You cannot finish them off quickly, or wild animals would become too numerous for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God will clear away these nations before you little by little. You will not be able to finish them quickly, lest the wild animals multiply against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine handing over, intensified confusion, and its stated endpoint.
verses.before: But the LORD your God will give them before you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
verses.after: The LORD your God will hand them over to you and throw them into utter panic until they are destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD your God will give them before you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.

verses.rationale: Retains the names-under-heaven image and the repeated destruction claim.
verses.before: He will give their kings into your hand, and you will cause their name to perish from under the heavens. No one will stand before you until you have destroyed them.
verses.after: He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will stand against you until you have destroyed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will give their kings into your hand, and you shall cause their name to perish from under the heavens. No one will stand before you until you have destroyed them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the specific temptation of valuable coverings and the recurring snare warning.
verses.before: “You will burn the carved images of their gods with fire. You will not desire the silver or gold that is on them or take it for yourself, lest you be snared by it, for it is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.
verses.after: Burn the carved images of their gods. Do not covet the silver or gold on them and take it for yourself, or it will become a snare to you. It is detestable to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall burn the carved images of their gods with fire. You shall not desire the silver or gold that is on them or take it for yourself, lest you be snared by it, for it is a detestable thing to the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the transfer of ban status to the possessor and the emphatic paired rejection.
verses.before: You will not bring a detestable thing into your house and become devoted to destruction like it. You will utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.
verses.after: Do not bring a detestable thing into your house, or you too will be devoted to destruction like it. Utterly detest it and abhor it, because it is devoted to destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bring a detestable thing into your house and become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps the comprehensive instruction and all four linked outcomes.
verses.before: Every commandment that I command you today you will keep to do, so that you may live and multiply and enter and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.
verses.after: “Be careful to practice this whole commandment that I give you today, so that you may live, become numerous, and enter and possess the land the LORD swore to your fathers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every commandment that I command you today you shall keep to do, so that you may live and multiply and enter and possess the land that the LORD swore to your fathers.

verses.rationale: Retains the stated purpose of knowing the heart without replacing it with a theological explanation; follows the read spelling of commands.
verses.before: And you will remember all the way that the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart—whether you would keep his commandments, his commandments, or not.
verses.after: Remember the whole way the LORD your God led you through the wilderness these forty years, to humble you and test you, to know what was in your heart—whether you would keep his commands or not.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall remember all the way that the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, to test you, to know what was in your heart—whether you would keep his commandments, his commandments, or not.

verses.rationale: Preserves hunger and provision together and the broad everything-from-mouth wording rather than narrowing it to an inserted word.
verses.before: And he humbled you and let you hunger and fed you manna, which you did not know and which your fathers did not know, in order to make you know that the human does not live by bread alone, but the human lives by every utterance from the mouth of the LORD.
verses.after: He humbled you, let you go hungry, and fed you manna, which neither you nor your fathers had known. He did this to teach you that a human being does not live on bread alone, but on everything that comes from the LORD's mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he humbled you and let you hunger and fed you manna, which you did not know and which your fathers did not know, in order to make you know that the human does not live by bread alone, but the human lives by every utterance from the mouth of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps both bodily provisions and the exact repeated duration.
verses.before: Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell, these forty years.
verses.after: Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell during these forty years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell, these forty years.

verses.rationale: Retains the specifically male family image and discipline as the comparison's action.
verses.before: And know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.
verses.after: Know in your heart that the LORD your God disciplines you as a man disciplines his son.
verses.tsw_comparator: And know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you.

verses.rationale: Preserves walking and fear rather than reducing both to a generic obedience term.
verses.before: And you will keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
verses.after: Keep the commands of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.

verses.rationale: Retains the three water descriptions and contrasting terrain within the extended land portrait.
verses.before: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land—a land of brooks of water, of springs and deep waters, flowing out in valleys and hills,
verses.after: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of flowing streams, springs, and deep waters welling up in valleys and hills,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land—a land of brooks of water, of springs and deep waters, flowing out in valleys and hills,

verses.rationale: Preserves all seven named produce types and the repeated land introduction.
verses.before: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,
verses.after: a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
verses.tsw_comparator: a land of wheat and barley, of vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,

verses.rationale: Keeps the promise of no lack and both mineral resources without modernizing their units or extraction.
verses.before: a land in which you will eat bread without scarcity, in which you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you can dig copper.
verses.after: a land where you will not eat bread in scarcity and will lack nothing, a land whose stones contain iron and from whose hills you can mine copper.
verses.tsw_comparator: a land in which you will eat bread without scarcity, in which you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you can dig copper.

verses.rationale: Preserves blessing God after satisfaction and connects it to the land gift.
verses.before: And you will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the LORD your God for the good land that he has given you.
verses.after: When you have eaten your fill, bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless the LORD your God for the good land that he has given you.

verses.rationale: Makes forgetting's connection to neglected practice explicit while retaining the three categories.
verses.before: Take care lest you forget the LORD your God by not keeping his commandments and his judgments and his statutes, which I command you today,
verses.after: Be careful not to forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, rulings, and statutes that I give you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take care lest you forget the LORD your God by not keeping his commandments and his judgments and his statutes, which I command you today,

verses.rationale: Begins the abundance condition without prematurely resolving the warning.
verses.before: lest, when you eat and are satisfied and build good houses and dwell in them,
verses.after: When you eat your fill, build good houses and live in them,
verses.tsw_comparator: lest, when you eat and are satisfied and build good houses and dwell in them,

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated increase and all three kinds of prosperity.
verses.before: and your herds and your flocks multiply and your silver and your gold multiply and all that you have multiplies,
verses.after: and your herds and flocks increase, your silver and gold increase, and everything you have increases,
verses.tsw_comparator: and your herds and your flocks multiply and your silver and your gold multiply and all that you have multiplies,

verses.rationale: Completes the warning with raised-heart pride and remembrance of slavery.
verses.before: then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
verses.after: do not let your heart grow proud and forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
verses.tsw_comparator: then your heart be lifted up, and you forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,

verses.rationale: Preserves fiery snakes as the ancient description and retains the arid setting and flint source.
verses.before: who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, with fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water, who brought you water out of the rock of flint,
verses.after: He led you through the vast, terrifying wilderness, with its fiery snakes and scorpions, its thirsty ground where there was no water. He brought water out of flint rock for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: who led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, with fiery serpents and scorpions and thirsty ground where there was no water, who brought you water out of the rock of flint,

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated manna, humiliation, and testing themes with their final beneficial purpose.
verses.before: who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, that he might humble you and that he might test you, to do you good in the end.
verses.after: He fed you manna in the wilderness, something your fathers had not known, to humble and test you, and in the end to do you good.
verses.tsw_comparator: who fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your fathers did not know, that he might humble you and that he might test you, to do you good in the end.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the warning's implied prohibition while retaining the self-crediting hand image.
verses.before: Beware lest you say in your heart, “My power and the strength of my hand have gotten me this wealth.”
verses.after: Do not say in your heart, ‘My power and the strength of my own hand have made this wealth for me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Beware lest you say in your heart, “My power and the strength of my hand have gotten me this wealth.”

verses.rationale: Keeps divine enabling and covenant fulfillment rather than turning the sentence into a general prosperity maxim.
verses.before: But you will remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.
verses.after: Remember the LORD your God, because he is the one who gives you the power to gain wealth, fulfilling his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as he is doing today.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you shall remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you power to get wealth, that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conditional warning, three actions of apostasy, and emphatic destruction.
verses.before: And it will be, if you forget—utterly forget—the LORD your God, and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you will surely perish.
verses.after: If you forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, serving them and bowing down to them, I testify against you today that you will surely perish.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it shall be, if you forget—utterly forget—the LORD your God, and go after other gods and serve them and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you shall surely perish.

verses.rationale: Retains the reversal of Israel's treatment of other nations back upon Israel.
verses.before: Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you will perish, because you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
verses.after: Like the nations the LORD is destroying before you, so you will perish, because you would not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you shall perish, because you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Renders today as the imminent crossing and keeps the fortification hyperbole.
verses.before: “Hear, Israel! You are crossing the Jordan today to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified to the heavens,
verses.after: “Hear, Israel! You are about to cross the Jordan to enter and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large towns fortified up to the heavens.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear, Israel! You are crossing the Jordan today to go in and dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, cities great and fortified to the heavens,

verses.rationale: Preserves both related people designations and the familiar fear-provoking question.
verses.before: a people great and tall, the children of the Anakim, whom you know and of whom you have heard it said, ‘Who can stand before the children of Anak?’
verses.after: Their people are great and tall, descendants of the Anakim. You know them, and you have heard it said, ‘Who can stand against the descendants of Anak?’
verses.tsw_comparator: a people great and tall, the children of the Anakim, whom you know and of whom you have heard it said, ‘Who can stand before the children of Anak?’

verses.rationale: Keeps the fire image, divine and human agency, and quick destruction without harmonizing 7:22.
verses.before: Know today that the LORD your God is the one crossing before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and subdue them before you, and you will dispossess them and cause them to perish quickly, as the LORD has spoken to you.
verses.after: Know today that the LORD your God is crossing ahead of you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and subdue them before you. You will drive them out and quickly destroy them, as the LORD promised you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know today that the LORD your God is the one crossing before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and subdue them before you, and you shall dispossess them and cause them to perish quickly, as the LORD has spoken to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the contrast between the rejected claim of righteousness and the stated wickedness of the nations.
verses.before: Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God has driven them out from before you, ‘Because of my righteousness the LORD brought me in to possess this land,’ when because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD is dispossessing them before you.
verses.after: When the LORD your God drives them out before you, do not say in your heart, ‘The LORD brought me in to possess this land because of my righteousness.’ It is because of these nations' wickedness that the LORD is driving them out before you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not say in your heart, when the LORD your God has driven them out from before you, ‘Because of my righteousness the LORD brought me in to possess this land,’ when because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD is dispossessing them before you.

verses.rationale: Preserves both rejected grounds and both stated grounds, with all three ancestors named.
verses.before: Not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you, and in order to establish the word that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.after: You are not entering to possess their land because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart. The LORD your God is driving these nations out before you because of their wickedness, and to fulfill the word he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart are you going in to possess their land, but because of the wickedness of these nations the LORD your God is dispossessing them before you, and in order to establish the word that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keeps the third denial of righteousness and the physical stubbornness image.
verses.before: Know therefore that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.
verses.after: Know this: the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness. You are a stiff-necked people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know therefore that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to possess because of your righteousness, for you are a stiff-necked people.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired memory commands and comprehensive accusation over the journey.
verses.before: “Remember; do not forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you came out from the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.
verses.after: Remember—do not forget—how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you left Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebellious toward the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Remember; do not forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you came out from the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit destructive intent rather than weakening it to displeasure.
verses.before: Even at Horeb you provoked the LORD, and the LORD was angry with you enough to destroy you.
verses.after: At Horeb you provoked the LORD, and he became angry enough with you to destroy you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even at Horeb you provoked the LORD, and the LORD was angry with you enough to destroy you.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant identification, both duration components, and both fasting restrictions.
verses.before: When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.
verses.after: When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.

verses.rationale: Preserves the finger-of-God image and the full correspondence with the assembled people's hearing.
verses.before: The LORD gave me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words that the LORD had spoken with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.
verses.after: The LORD gave me the two stone tablets written with the finger of God. On them were all the words the LORD spoke to you on the mountain from the fire, on the day of the assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gave me the two tablets of stone written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words that the LORD had spoken with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated duration and tablet description rather than treating the repetition as expendable.
verses.before: At the end of forty days and forty nights the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.
verses.after: At the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of forty days and forty nights the LORD gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps God's your people and you brought out attribution, as well as repeated haste and the cast image.
verses.before: “Then the LORD said to me, ‘Rise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out from Egypt have corrupted themselves. They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image.’
verses.after: Then the LORD told me, ‘Get up and go down quickly from here. Your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They have quickly turned from the way I commanded them and made themselves a cast image.’
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then the LORD said to me, ‘Rise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out from Egypt have corrupted themselves. They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a cast image.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the divine assessment and repeated bodily image.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to me, saying, ‘I have seen this people, and look, it is a stiff-necked people.
verses.after: The LORD also told me, ‘I have seen this people. They are a stiff-necked people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to me, saying, ‘I have seen this people, and look, it is a stiff-necked people.

verses.rationale: Keeps the destructive proposal and the alternative nation through Moses as direct speech.
verses.before: Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I will make from you a nation mightier and more numerous than they.’
verses.after: Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and more numerous than they are.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under the heavens, and I will make from you a nation mightier and more numerous than they.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the fiery setting and the paired two tablets and two hands.
verses.before: So I turned and came down from the mountain while the mountain burned with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
verses.after: I turned and came down the mountain while it was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I turned and came down from the mountain while the mountain burned with fire, and the two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.

verses.rationale: Retains the specific calf and the repeated quick departure from the commanded path.
verses.before: I saw, and look, you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made for yourselves a cast calf. You had quickly turned aside from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
verses.after: I looked and saw that you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves a cast calf and quickly turned from the way the LORD commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw, and look, you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made for yourselves a cast calf. You had quickly turned aside from the way that the LORD had commanded you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three actions and the people's witnessing of the broken tablets.
verses.before: I took hold of the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.
verses.after: I took hold of the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I took hold of the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and shattered them before your eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated fasting and duration without imposing a reconstructed chronology.
verses.before: Then I fell down before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all your sin that you had committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke him to anger.
verses.after: Then I lay prostrate before the LORD as before, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all the sin you had committed, doing evil in the LORD's eyes and provoking him to anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I fell down before the LORD as at the first, forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all your sin that you had committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke him to anger.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses' fear and the contrast with the repeated divine hearing.
verses.before: For I was afraid of the anger and fury with which the LORD was angry against you to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time also.
verses.after: I was afraid of the anger and fury with which the LORD raged against you, ready to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time too.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I was afraid of the anger and fury with which the LORD was angry against you to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time also.

verses.rationale: Keeps Aaron's particular danger and Moses' intercession for him.
verses.before: The LORD was very angry with Aaron and would have destroyed him, but I prayed for Aaron also at that time.
verses.after: The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron too at that time.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD was very angry with Aaron and would have destroyed him, but I prayed for Aaron also at that time.

verses.rationale: Unfolds your sin as the made object while retaining every destruction stage and the stream disposal.
verses.before: Then I took your sin, the calf that you had made, and burned it with fire and crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust. I threw its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.
verses.after: I took that sinful thing you had made, the calf, and burned it. I crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and threw its dust into the stream flowing down the mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I took your sin, the calf that you had made, and burned it with fire and crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust. I threw its dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three named events in their stated order.
verses.before: “At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-Hattaavah you provoked the LORD.
verses.after: At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you provoked the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-Hattaavah you provoked the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the quoted command and threefold failure of rebellion, trust, and hearing.
verses.before: And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-Barnea, saying, ‘Go up and possess the land that I have given you,’ you rebelled against the mouth of the LORD your God and did not trust him or listen to his voice.
verses.after: When the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said, ‘Go up and possess the land I have given you,’ you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-Barnea, saying, ‘Go up and possess the land that I have given you,’ you rebelled against the mouth of the LORD your God and did not trust him or listen to his voice.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses' first-person temporal accusation without softening its breadth.
verses.before: You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.
verses.after: You have been rebellious toward the LORD ever since I have known you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day I knew you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the retrospective resumption of the prostration rather than automatically counting another forty days.
verses.before: “So I fell down before the LORD the forty days and forty nights that I fell down, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
verses.after: So I lay prostrate before the LORD for those forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “So I fell down before the LORD the forty days and forty nights that I fell down, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prayer's reversal to your people and inheritance, along with redemption and strong hand.
verses.before: I prayed to the LORD and said, ‘Lord GOD, do not destroy your people and your inheritance whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out from Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.after: I prayed to the LORD, ‘Lord GOD, do not destroy your people, your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a strong hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: I prayed to the LORD and said, ‘Lord GOD, do not destroy your people and your inheritance whom you redeemed by your greatness, whom you brought out from Egypt with a strong hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the named servants and the three things Moses asks God not to regard.
verses.before: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not turn toward the stubbornness of this people or toward their wickedness or their sin,
verses.after: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at this people's stubbornness, wickedness, or sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not turn toward the stubbornness of this people or toward their wickedness or their sin,

verses.rationale: Makes the land's people explicit and uses reported speech to keep the nested accusation of inability and hatred clear.
verses.before: lest the land from which you brought us say, “Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land that he spoke to them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to put them to death in the wilderness.”
verses.after: Otherwise the people of the land you brought us from will say that the LORD could not bring them into the land he promised them, and that he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness because he hated them.
verses.tsw_comparator: lest the land from which you brought us say, “Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land that he spoke to them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to put them to death in the wilderness.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated closing appeal to ownership and the liberation image.
verses.before: Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.’
verses.after: Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and outstretched arm.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.’

verses.rationale: Keeps both commanded objects and the ascent in the order given.
verses.before: “At that time the LORD said to me, ‘Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Make for yourself an ark of wood.
verses.after: “At that time the LORD told me, ‘Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up the mountain to me. Also make yourself a wooden ark.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At that time the LORD said to me, ‘Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Make for yourself an ark of wood.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine writing, Moses' breaking, and the instruction for storage.
verses.before: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets that you shattered, and you will put them in the ark.’
verses.after: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered. Put them in the ark.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets that you shattered, and you shall put them in the ark.’

verses.rationale: Retains Moses' first-person construction account, wood type, and paired tablets without harmonizing Exodus' artisan account.
verses.before: So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
verses.after: So I made an ark of acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.

verses.rationale: Makes the writer explicit while preserving the repeated words and assembled setting.
verses.before: He wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the Ten Words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly. Then the LORD gave them to me.
verses.after: The LORD wrote on the tablets what he had written before: the Ten Words he spoke to you on the mountain from the fire, on the day of the assembly. Then he gave them to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: He wrote on the tablets, like the first writing, the Ten Words that the LORD had spoken to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly. Then the LORD gave them to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the descent, deposit, and continuing location of the tablets.
verses.before: I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made, and there they are, as the LORD commanded me.
verses.after: I turned and came down the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made. They are still there, as the LORD commanded me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark that I had made, and there they are, as the LORD commanded me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the route and stated place of Aaron's death without changing it to match Numbers 33.
verses.before: “The children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.
verses.after: The Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. Aaron died and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest in his place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated station and the water-rich destination.
verses.before: From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
verses.after: From there they traveled to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of flowing streams.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.

verses.rationale: Retains all three functions assigned collectively to Levi without inserting later subdivisions into this statement.
verses.before: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
verses.after: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the LORD's covenant, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to bless in his name, as they do to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to minister to him, and to bless in his name, to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between territorial share and the LORD as inheritance.
verses.before: So Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God spoke concerning him.
verses.after: That is why Levi has no share or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God promised him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore Levi has no portion or inheritance with his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God spoke concerning him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the duration and repeated hearing without resolving the retrospective sequence into a new timetable.
verses.before: “And I stayed on the mountain as at the first, forty days and forty nights. The LORD listened to me that time also; the LORD was not willing to destroy you.
verses.after: I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had the first time. The LORD listened to me that time too; he was not willing to destroy you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And I stayed on the mountain as at the first, forty days and forty nights. The LORD listened to me that time also; the LORD was not willing to destroy you.

verses.rationale: Unfolds going before as leadership while preserving the sworn land purpose.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to me, ‘Rise, go on the journey before the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.’
verses.after: The LORD told me, ‘Get up and lead the people on their journey, so that they may enter and possess the land I swore to their fathers to give them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to me, ‘Rise, go on the journey before the people, so that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.’

verses.rationale: Unfolds the rhetorical question while retaining every requested response and both total-devotion terms.
verses.before: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask from you except to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your life,
verses.after: Now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? Only this: fear the LORD your God, walk in all his ways, love him, and serve the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask from you except to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your life,

verses.rationale: Completes the list with keeping and its stated benefit rather than separating it from the question.
verses.before: to keep the commandments of the LORD and his statutes that I command you today for your good?
verses.after: keeping the LORD's commands and statutes that I give you today for your good.
verses.tsw_comparator: to keep the commandments of the LORD and his statutes that I command you today for your good?

verses.rationale: Retains heavens of heavens as an expansive superlative and the total earthly claim.
verses.before: Look, to the LORD your God belong the heavens and the heavens of heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
verses.after: Look, the heavens, even the highest heavens, belong to the LORD your God, along with the earth and everything in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, to the LORD your God belong the heavens and the heavens of heavens, the earth and all that is in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast between universal ownership and particular affection and choice.
verses.before: Yet the LORD set his affection upon your ancestors to love them, and he chose their offspring after them—you—from all the peoples, as it is this day.
verses.after: Yet the LORD set his affection on your fathers and loved them. He chose their descendants after them—you—out of all peoples, as he has done today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the LORD set his affection upon your ancestors to love them, and he chose their offspring after them—you—from all the peoples, as it is this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the paired bodily metaphors rather than replacing them entirely with psychological explanation.
verses.before: “So circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.
verses.after: Circumcise your hearts, then, and no longer stiffen your necks.
verses.tsw_comparator: “So circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not stiffen your neck any longer.

verses.rationale: Retains the titles and three attributes, rendering the face-lifting idiom as impartiality.
verses.before: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and fearsome God, who does not show partiality and does not take a bribe.
verses.after: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and fearsome God. He shows no favoritism and accepts no bribe.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and fearsome God, who does not show partiality and does not take a bribe.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three specifically vulnerable groups and love expressed in concrete provision.
verses.before: He executes justice for the orphan and the widow and loves the resident alien, giving him food and clothing.
verses.after: He upholds justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the resident foreigner, giving that person food and clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: He executes justice for the orphan and the widow and loves the resident alien, giving him food and clothing.

verses.rationale: Preserves the command's repeated love and its grounding in Israel's own experience.
verses.before: So you will love the resident alien, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
verses.after: You too must love the resident foreigner, because you were resident foreigners in Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you shall love the resident alien, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retains all four imperatives, including the physical cling image and oath-taking.
verses.before: The LORD your God you will fear; him you will serve; to him you will cling; and by his name you will swear.
verses.after: Fear the LORD your God, serve him, cling to him, and swear by his name.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD your God you shall fear; him you shall serve; to him you shall cling; and by his name you shall swear.

verses.rationale: Keeps the praise designation and eyewitness appeal without replacing the ancient expression with explanation.
verses.before: He is your praise, and he is your God, who did for you these great and fearsome things that your eyes have seen.
verses.after: He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and fearsome things your eyes have seen.
verses.tsw_comparator: He is your praise, and he is your God, who did for you these great and fearsome things that your eyes have seen.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact seventy-person starting point and stars comparison.
verses.before: Your ancestors went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the heavens.
verses.after: Your fathers went down to Egypt as seventy people. Now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your ancestors went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Keeps love joined to enduring practice and all instruction categories.
verses.before: “You will love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments, and his commandments all the days.
verses.after: “Love the LORD your God and always keep what he requires—his statutes, rulings, and commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall love the LORD your God and keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments, and his commandments all the days.

verses.rationale: Supplies the implied speaking contrast to make the elliptical sentence understandable while retaining the generation distinction.
verses.before: Know today—for I am not speaking with your children who have not known and have not seen—the discipline of the LORD your God: his greatness, his strong hand, and his outstretched arm;
verses.after: Take this to heart today. I am speaking to you, not to your children, who did not know or see the discipline of the LORD your God, his greatness, his strong hand and outstretched arm.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know today—for I am not speaking with your children who have not known and have not seen—the discipline of the LORD your God: his greatness, his strong hand, and his outstretched arm;

verses.rationale: Carries the preceding children contrast through the list while preserving the specific targets.
verses.before: his signs and his deeds that he did among Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land;
verses.after: They did not see his signs and the deeds he did in Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and his whole land,
verses.tsw_comparator: his signs and his deeds that he did in the midst of Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land;

verses.rationale: Retains the military details, pursuit, inundation, and continuing force of the to-this-day claim.
verses.before: and what he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and chariots, how he made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them when they pursued you, and the LORD destroyed them to this day;
verses.after: or what he did to Egypt's army, its horses and chariots—how he swept the waters of the Sea of Reeds over them as they pursued you. The LORD destroyed them, and that destruction stands to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: and what he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and chariots, how he made the waters of the Sea of Reeds flow over them when they pursued you, and the LORD destroyed them to this day;

verses.rationale: Maintains the rhetorical contrast without adding new events to the summary.
verses.before: and what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place;
verses.after: They did not see what he did for you in the wilderness until you reached this place,
verses.tsw_comparator: and what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place;

verses.rationale: Preserves the named ancestry, earth-mouth image, and full list of swallowed dependents; notes the final expression's range.
verses.before: and what he did to Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, among all Israel.
verses.after: or what he did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, a descendant of Reuben: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: and what he did to Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab son of Reuben, how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and every living thing that followed them, in the midst of all Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the emphatic return to the eyewitness audience after the extended contrast.
verses.before: For your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did.
verses.after: Your own eyes saw all the great deeds the LORD did.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your own eyes have seen all the great work of the LORD that he did.

verses.rationale: Retains the whole commandment, strength, and deliberate repeated possession language.
verses.before: “So you will keep all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strong and go in and possess the land that you are crossing over to possess,
verses.after: So keep this whole commandment that I give you today, so that you may be strong and enter and possess the land you are crossing over to possess,
verses.tsw_comparator: “So you shall keep all the commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strong and go in and possess the land that you are crossing over to possess,

verses.rationale: Completes the purpose chain with long life, descendants, and the land image.
verses.before: and so that you may prolong your days upon the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.after: and so that you may live long on the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: and so that you may prolong your days upon the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual foot-irrigation expression and explains its uncertain mechanism in a note rather than substituting hand.
verses.before: “For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot like a vegetable garden.
verses.after: The land you are entering to possess is not like Egypt, which you left. There you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, like a vegetable garden.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For the land that you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot like a vegetable garden.

verses.rationale: Keeps the land's drinking image and the contrast with Egyptian irrigation.
verses.before: But the land that you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys. From the rain of the heavens it drinks water,
verses.after: But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys that drinks water from the rain of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the land that you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys. From the rain of the heavens it drinks water,

verses.rationale: Preserves divine care and eyes through the entire annual cycle.
verses.before: a land that the LORD your God seeks after. The eyes of the LORD your God are continually upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
verses.after: It is a land the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to its end.
verses.tsw_comparator: a land that the LORD your God seeks after. The eyes of the LORD your God are continually upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.

verses.rationale: Uses quotation to mark the divine promise that follows while retaining the source's first- and third-person divine references.
verses.before: “And it will be, if you diligently listen to my commandments that I command you today, to love the LORD your God and serve him with all your heart and with all your life,
verses.after: ‘If you listen carefully to my commands that I give you today, loving the LORD your God and serving him with all your heart and all your soul,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And it will be, if you diligently listen to my commandments that I command you today, to love the LORD your God and serve him with all your heart and with all your life,

verses.rationale: Preserves I will rather than silently changing it to he will and makes the two agricultural rain seasons clear.
verses.before: then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, so that you may gather your grain, new wine, and oil.
verses.after: I will give rain for your land in its season, the autumn rain and the spring rain, so that you may gather your grain, new wine, and oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the later rain, so that you may gather your grain, new wine, and oil.

verses.rationale: Keeps pasture and human satisfaction within the quoted promise.
verses.before: I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
verses.after: I will provide grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat your fill.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.

verses.rationale: Retains inward enticement and its outward actions without adding a modern psychological diagnosis.
verses.before: Guard yourselves, lest your heart be deceived and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.
verses.after: Watch yourselves, so that your hearts are not enticed and you turn away to serve other gods and bow down to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Guard yourselves, lest your heart be deceived and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the causal sequence of anger, closed heavens, crop failure, and perishing.
verses.before: Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and he will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain and the ground does not give its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you.
verses.after: Then the LORD's anger would burn against you. He would shut up the heavens so there would be no rain and the ground would give no harvest, and you would quickly perish from the good land the LORD is giving you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and he will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain and the ground does not give its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the embodied wording and matches the earlier bands rendering without suppressing the rare term's uncertainty.
verses.before: “You will put these words of mine on your heart and on your life. Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they will be as frontlets between your eyes.
verses.after: Place these words of mine on your heart and soul. Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be bands between your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall put these words of mine on your heart and on your life. Bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains the four daily settings and the recurring teaching pattern from chapter 6.
verses.before: Teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise.
verses.after: Teach them to your children. Speak of them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Teach them to your children, speaking of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise.

verses.rationale: Keeps both writing locations and lets the purpose follow across the verse boundary.
verses.before: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
verses.after: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
verses.tsw_comparator: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,

verses.rationale: Preserves the intergenerational promise and the cosmic duration comparison.
verses.before: so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied upon the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.
verses.after: so that your days and your children's days in the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give them may be many, as long as the heavens are over the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied upon the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them, as the days of the heavens above the earth.

verses.rationale: Retains the condition and its three descriptions, including clinging, into the outcome.
verses.before: “For if you diligently keep all this commandment that I command you to do, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cling to him,
verses.after: If you are careful to practice this whole commandment that I give you—loving the LORD your God, walking in all his ways, and clinging to him—
verses.tsw_comparator: “For if you diligently keep all this commandment that I command you to do, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cling to him,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine displacement followed by human dispossession and comparative strength.
verses.before: then the LORD will dispossess all these nations from before you, and you will possess nations greater and mightier than you.
verses.after: the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the LORD will dispossess all these nations from before you, and you will possess nations greater and mightier than you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sole image and all four territorial limits without importing a modern map.
verses.before: Every place on which the sole of your foot treads will be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River, the Euphrates River, as far as the western sea, will be your territory.
verses.after: Every place the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your boundary will run from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the river, the Euphrates, to the western sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, from the River, the Euphrates River, as far as the western sea, shall be your territory.

verses.rationale: Retains the assurance and paired fear terms with the repeated treading image.
verses.before: No one will stand before you. The LORD your God will put the dread and fear of you upon all the land on which you tread, as he spoke to you.
verses.after: No one will stand against you. The LORD your God will put fear and dread of you over all the land you tread, as he promised you.
verses.tsw_comparator: No one will stand before you. The LORD your God will put the dread and fear of you upon all the land on which you tread, as he spoke to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the see imperative and balanced alternatives as the section's opening.
verses.before: “See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
verses.after: See, today I am setting before you a blessing and a curse.
verses.tsw_comparator: “See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:

verses.rationale: Makes the condition explicit while keeping the instruction's present address.
verses.before: the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today;
verses.after: The blessing is yours if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I give you today.
verses.tsw_comparator: the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today;

verses.rationale: Preserves the negative condition, path departure, and unfamiliar gods.
verses.before: and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God but turn aside from the way that I command you today to go after other gods whom you have not known.
verses.after: The curse is yours if you do not listen to the commands of the LORD your God, but turn from the way I command you today to follow other gods you have not known.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the LORD your God but turn aside from the way that I command you today to go after other gods whom you have not known.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct mountain assignments and the action of placing the pronouncements there.
verses.before: And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, you will place the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
verses.after: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to possess, you shall place the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

verses.rationale: Retains every geographical marker and the rhetorical question while noting the compressed route description's uncertainty.
verses.before: Are they not beyond the Jordan, toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
verses.after: Are they not beyond the Jordan, west of the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are they not beyond the Jordan, toward the setting of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated possession and the movement toward settled residence.
verses.before: For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
verses.after: For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land the LORD your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you. You shall possess it and live in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the concluding practical instruction and its two categories.
verses.before: So you will be careful to do all the statutes and judgments that I set before you today.
verses.after: Be careful to practice all the statutes and rulings I am setting before you today.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So you shall be careful to do all the statutes and judgments that I set before you today.

verses.rationale: Keeps the enduring duration and land-ground setting of the laws.
verses.before: “These are the statutes and judgments that you will be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, all the days that you live upon the ground.
verses.after: “These are the statutes and rulings you must be careful to practice in the land the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess, all the days you live on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: “These are the statutes and judgments that you shall be careful to do in the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, all the days that you live upon the ground.

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive destruction and all three cultic settings.
verses.before: You will surely destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every flourishing tree.
verses.after: Completely destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods—on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall surely destroy all the places where the nations whom you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every flourishing tree.

verses.rationale: Keeps every object and action, preserving this chapter's burn/cut order distinct from 7:5.
verses.before: You will tear down their altars, shatter their pillars, burn their Asherah poles with fire, cut down the carved images of their gods, and destroy their name from that place.
verses.after: Tear down their altars, smash their standing stones, burn their Asherah poles, cut down the carved images of their gods, and wipe out their names from those places.
